hdd3_5.note: Standard 3.5in HDD 101.6 x 26.11 x 146.05 mm (SFF-8301 defines it; the SFF PDF was not read). Typical weight ~0.6-0.7 kg not verified.

drive2_5.note: Wikipedia table gives length 4.0 in (101.6 mm). SFF-8201 itself is often quoted at 100.45 mm max length; not verified here. 7 mm = SATA SSD/thin HDD, 9.5 mm = laptop HDD, 15 mm = enterprise U.2/high-capacity.

m2.note: Not researched; M.2 sizes are named WWLL in mm (2280 = 22 x 80 mm).

rack19.holeSpacingNote: Within a U the holes are 6.35, 22.25, 38.1 mm from the U edge, so 15.9 + 15.9 inside the U and 12.7 across the U boundary (6.35 + 6.35). The U boundary sits in the middle of the 12.7 mm (1/2 in) gap.
rack19.fasteners: Tapped rails usually 10-32 UNF, less often M6; square-hole rails take cage nuts (M6 most common in Europe, 10-32 / 12-24 in the US).
rack19.standard: EIA-310 (current revision reported as -D or -E; not confirmed)
rack19.note: Wikipedia: panel 482.6, posts 15.88 wide with 450.85 gap, hole pairs 464.2-465.8 mm centre-to-centre, holes at 6.35/22.25/38.1 mm in each 44.45 mm unit, 1U panel 43.7 mm. 465.1 (18.312 in) nominal from RackSolutions help page (search snippet).

rack10.note: Lab Rax article (verified): 44.45 mm unit, holes 236.525 mm apart, 222 mm usable between posts. 254 mm panel and 222.25 mm (8.75 in) opening from micropolis rack FAQ and others (search snippets). Same vertical hole pattern and 15.875 mm rails as 19in. Gotcha: 2020-extrusion racks give 222 mm between rails but 242 mm screw-to-screw (MackRack note), so 236.525 mm panels need slotted holes there. Jeff Geerling's Project Mini Rack quotes ~210 mm usable width for gear.

printersNote: Bambu Lab pages (bambulab.com, store, wiki) refused automated fetches, so all Bambu values are third-party and unverified; Polymaker's wiki wrongly lists the A1 mini as 160 mm, the 180 mm figure is from several other sources. H2D 350x320x325 is the single-nozzle figure; usable area with both nozzles is smaller (not verified). Prusa CORE One L (300x300x330) is a separate model. Ender-3 V3 Plus is 300x300x330.

printableRacks.name: Lab Rax (Michael Klements / the-diy-life)
printableRacks.railConstruction: Fully printed 10in frame: 4 vertical posts printed in 1U-5U sections (two sections stack to 10U), 4 edge pieces, 4 horizontal pieces, feet, handles, optional side/top panels (or 3 mm acrylic/plywood). Designed for ~250 mm beds (author used 256x256); main cross member does not fit 220 mm beds (split version announced).
printableRacks.hardware: Insert version: 24x M6x10 button-head screws + 24x M6 brass inserts 8 mm OD, 4 or 5 mm long for the frame, plus 6 inserts per U for equipment. Bolted version (no inserts): 16x M6x12 button-head + 16x M6 nuts, or #10-32 x 1/2 screws + #10-32 nuts. Hole spacing 236.525 mm, 222 mm between posts.
printableRacks.material: PETG recommended (PLA OK for low heat). 5U frame ~580 g, side panels ~360 g; 1 kg spool covers frame + panels.
printableRacks.note: Details verified on https://the-diy-life.com/introducing-lab-rax-a-3d-printable-modular-10-rack-system/ . Licence not stated in the article; MakerWorld page blocked. Variants: 4U, 6U, split front panel, 19in remix, wall mount.

printableRacks.name: Modular 10in rack (bwees)
printableRacks.railConstruction: Fully printed; modular rail sections of varying length joined to reach any height.
printableRacks.hardware: Standard button-head M6x12 bolts and M6 square nuts (no heat-set inserts).
printableRacks.note: Hardware from a search snippet of the Printables page; page itself blocked (403), material and licence unverified. Listed on Jeff Geerling's Project Mini Rack.

printableRacks.name: rackstack (jazwa)
printableRacks.railConstruction: Fully printed, parametric OpenSCAD (rbuild.py generates sizes; prebuilt STLs ~200 mm 'mini', 180 'micro', 100 'nano'). Parts: Y-bars, X-bars, 4 main rails, side walls, XY plates, feet; stackable with printed rackJoiners. Not strictly 10in EIA.
printableRacks.hardware: Per rack: 12x M3x12 + 16x M3x16 flat-head screws, 28x M3 hex nuts, 4x 3x10 mm steel dowel pins, 8x 6x2 mm neodymium magnets, super glue. Front rails take M4 for rack-mount items. Stacking: 4 joiners, 8x M3 nuts, 8x M3x12.
printableRacks.material: PLA/PETG/ABS, higher infill; print the tolerance test first.

printableRacks.name: KevsRobots 10in Mini Rack (2020 extrusion)
printableRacks.railConstruction: Four 20x20 mm aluminium extrusions cut to length, with printed corners (1U/2U/top/bottom), handle and Pi trays; laser-cut basswood top/front panels. 4U, 4 shelves 200 mm deep.
printableRacks.hardware: M6 rack nuts and bolts, M6 T-nuts for the handle; extrusion ends tapped M6. Print structural parts at 100% infill.
printableRacks.material: PLA (not named explicitly), aluminium extrusion, basswood.
printableRacks.note: STL/DXF on the page; site footer 'All rights reserved', no open licence. Other 2020 designs (MakerWorld 1081353, 'modrack') use M5 bolts/T-nuts with tapped M5 ends and 220 mm front cross pieces.

printableRacks.name: HomeRacker (kellervater)
printableRacks.railConstruction: Printed 15 mm square supports in multiples of 15 mm, joined by printed connectors and 4 mm printed lock pins; 10in standard in use, 19in in progress.
printableRacks.hardware: Tool-less; no screws for the frame (printed lock pins). Rack screws for gear not specified.
printableRacks.material: Tested with Bambu PLA Matte/Basic and ABS on textured PEI.
printableRacks.note: Code MIT, models CC BY-SA 4.0 (some MakerWorld models more restrictive).
